title: Same Tree
statement:
Decide whether two binary trees are identical in both shape and values.

Contract
- Either argument may be null. Nodes have an integer `value` and nullable `left` and `right` children.
- Return true only when both trees are empty, or when their roots hold equal values and their left subtrees match and their right subtrees match.
- A node that is a left child in one tree is not equal to the same value placed as a right child in the other. Do not modify either tree.
- Trees may be lopsided, with a height of up to 1000 nodes.

Examples
- `[1, 2, 3]` and `[1, 2, 3]` are the same.
- `[1, 2]` and `[1, null, 2]` have the same values on different sides, so they differ.
- `[1, 2, 3]` and `[1, 2, 4]` differ in one value.
hints: Compare the two roots first, then ask the same question about each pair of matching children.
Handle the cases where both nodes are null, only one is null, and both exist before looking at values.

Each node pair is visited at most once. Intended complexity: O(n) time where n is the node count of the smaller tree. Space is the recursion depth: O(h) for tree height h, which is O(log n) for a balanced tree (the workload uses balanced trees) and O(n) for a chain.
inputSyntax: Input: two level-order trees separated by a semicolon, for example: [1, 2, 3]; [1, 2, 3]
